existingStructuredCoverageCandidates.evidence: Inspected the actual batch-4 supplier Definitions/Statements and complete relevant Proofs. def-cardinal-polynomial-interpolation defines omega_n, w_j, ell_j, and I_n y=sum_j y_j ell_j for n>=0 and strictly increasing distinct real nodes. lem-cardinal-basis-degree-and-values proves the ell_j are degree-n polynomials and ell_j(x_i)=delta_ij (proof steps 1.1-1.2); its hypotheses include the nonzero denominator products. thm-cardinal-polynomial-interpolant-exists-uniquely proves I_n y exists and is the unique degree-at-most-n interpolant: step 1.1 establishes existence and node values, while step 2.1 applies the root bound to the n+1 distinct nodes and a degree-at-most-n difference. Reproduction I_n p=p follows by applying uniqueness to the data y_j=p(x_j), since p itself interpolates those values; batch 19 also proves reproduction locally in lem-cardinal-lagrange-interpolation-and-operator-norm. The batch-4 interface lists nodes in increasing order, while the Chebyshev angles in batch 19 list cosines in decreasing order. Reversing indices x_tilde_k=x_{n-k} gives the supplier convention; the product and sum are unchanged under the same data permutation, and the batch-19 local proof works directly in its stated order. The supplier theorem uses exactly the n+1 distinct-root hypothesis. No finite-precision stability claim is asserted or imported. The relevant batch-4 supplier proofs pass scoped precheck (2/2), proof-layout (2 items, 8 steps, 0 defects), strict proof-contract checking (2/2), the batch-4 dependency-level computation (15 items, maximum level 6), and batch-4 source-fetch verification (2/2 sources resolved). These authoring checks do not constitute independent approval. The best-error corollary is a Weierstrass argument and the equispaced Runge example proves its complex-pole identity locally; neither uses this interpolation interface as a premise. The declared page-level prerequisite nevertheless applies to the pair and companion.
